speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to help me determine the cause, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and how often you are urinating per day?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of dysuria, frequency, and nocturia that improve with voiding, combined with dyspareunia in a 40-year-old female, strongly suggest interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome or a chronic urinary tract infection. Given that NSAIDs and fluid restriction have failed, do you have any history of urinary tract infections or blood in your urine? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, and CBC.
